normalized.description: The ESA Antenna Laboratory operates several unique antenna and RF material measurement facilities, including the Sub-mmWave Scanner(SMS), LORENTZ cryogenic near-field scanner, and CATR Material Characterisation Facility. These facilities support antenna and RF characterisation activities covering a frequency range extending from microwave to sub-millimetre-wave frequencies and are routinely used in support of ESA programmes, technology developments, industrial activities and research campaigns.Operation ofthese facilities relies on dedicated custom-developed software that interfaces with motion control systems, network analysers and auxiliary equipment to perform automated measurements, collect measurement data and generate outputs suitable for post-processing andanalysis. Overthe past decade, this software has evolved through multiple development and maintenance activities, supporting successive laboratory upgrades and increasingly demanding measurement campaigns. The software currently comprises three principal application domains:            SMS scanner control software.            LORENTZ scanner control software.            CATR Material Characterisation control software.In addition, a growing set of shared software components has been introduced to provide common functionality across facilities, including hardware abstraction, configuration management, measurement orchestration, data management and graphical user interfaces. Historically, software development activities were executed through a number of independent projects. Consequently, different facilities evolved at different rates and software versions diverged over time. Recent maintenance activities have established a common software management approach based on GitLab repositories, issue tracking mechanisms and shared software components, improving traceability and maintainability of the software assets. The LORENTZ and CATR applications now share a modern architecture built around common software libraries and hardware abstraction layers. The SMS software remains operational but is based on anearlier architecture and represents the principal remaining source of technical debt within the software suite. Long-term sustainability of the Antenna Laboratory software therefore requires continued maintenance, harmonisation and progressive migration towards acommon software framework.The software environment further depends on several third-party components, including software drivers and interfaces fromKeysight, ACS Motion Control, Trio Motion Technology and other equipment suppliers. Maintaining compatibility withcommercial operating systems, hardware drivers and measurement instruments is therefore an essential part of maintaining the operational capability of the Antenna Laboratory. As several ESA facilities depend on the availability, reliability and traceability of measurement data,particular attention must be given to configuration control, software version management, measurement file compatibility and preservation of laboratory know-how. The software shall therefore be maintained as an operational laboratory asset rather than as a standalone development project.- Objective(s) of the ActivityThe objective of the activity is to ensure the continuous operation, maintenance, evolution and long-term sustainability of the Antenna Laboratory software systems, while preserving compatibility with existing facilities, measurement workflows and historical measurement data.

originalText: {"job":"institution-ESA-issued-competition","collectionState":"reconciled","verifiedOpen":false,"spaceRelevance":"not_assessed","recordType":"discovery_candidate","evidence":{"file":"institution-ESA-issued-competition/page-1-e4c5ccb5d8b8fe0909d8b83b39e2c5780b24a51cc88eeace783c79f2d32d3881.json","sha256":"e4c5ccb5d8b8fe0909d8b83b39e2c5780b24a51cc88eeace783c79f2d32d3881","row":14,"retrievedAt":"2026-10-20T13:39:22.053Z"},"original":{"activityNumber":"1000046331","closingDate":"2026-11-30T13:00:00","clarificationRequestDeadline":"2026-11-16T13:00:00","description":"To derive more accurate expression of atmosphere irregularities effects with a focus on the ionosphere, and devise mitigation techniques for both geo- and sun-synchronous SAR imaging systemsDescription: For Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) systems the atmospheric turbulence is generally assumed to be time-invariant during the synthetic aperture time due to itsshort duration. Such assumption is not always correct, as horizontal atmospheric drifts and vortices exist. Especially for SAR systems at low frequency (P-Band, L-Band), SAR operating on repeat-track basis, geo-synchronous SAR systems characterised by long integration time and extensive imaging scene, the ionosphere can have an important role on the performance. Furthermore, both temporal andspatial variations of the ionosphere have to be jointly taken into account, which further complicates their characterisation. Therefore, the effects of the flowing ionospheric irregularities need to be investigated, aiming in particular to image shifts, defocusing and repeat-track interferometry. The aim of this activity is to provide a comprehensive analysis to evaluate effects of both spatial variation and flowing ionospheric irregularities on SAR systems operating both at P-, L- and C-band. normalized.description: The frontiers for the deployment of 5G cellular networks have grown beyond the limits of the Earth's atmosphere. The 3GPP cellular technologies have become attractive for exploration missions, such as Moon or Mars, as they can provide a standardised scalable, secure, high-capacity, and reliable connectivity. For Moon, the Space Frequency Coordination Group (SFCG) has recently identified several bands for Lunar missions for the deployment of existing Earth communication protocols that includes the cellular element. In parallel to the connectivity, 5G networks can also be used to enhance the performance of navigation services fores een in LunaNet.The communication services will be primarily delivered by satellite-based solutions (already identified in the LunaNet architecture for the Moon). However, although the lunar relay satellites could technically provide surface-to-surface communications for a small number of users, such approach does not scale well as the number of users increases.To serve larger number of users, wireless cellularnetworks on the lunar surface are foreseen. With such deployments, an opportunity to offer 5G space user terminals emerges on the market. A new space-grade 5G user terminal will thus need to be developed, leveraging the technologies from 5G ground terminals, and making them available for exploration missions. This activity will design, manufacture, and test an engineering model of a 5G user terminal in FR1 for exploration missions. To achieve this, the activity willleverage on the current standards, techniques, and technologies. normalized.title: GT1I-805GA SECURITY FRAMEWORK FOR AI APPLICATIONS (EXPRO+)
normalized.description: Increasingly, advances in AI applications, models, and big data capabilities are making their way intoproductive applications. Roadmaps exist to introduce AI technologies into critical functional and operationaldomains. With new technology spin-ins like AI, cybersecurity must be accounted for, considering new attacksurfaces and vulnerabilities. Currently, no specialized approach exists forsystems with AI components,necessitating an ad-hoc approach for each system. To avoid redundant efforts, a coherent security approachfor AI applications in the space domain should be defined. Common mitigation measures for identified threatsand risks related to data and models need to be integrated into the AI lifecycle, ensuring a secure and AIenabledinfrastructure. Systems today demand increased security and even security certification. Whilesecurity approaches for non-AI systems are well understood, AI components introduce new threats. Thisactivity will guide developers in creating secure AI systems and assist project teams with certificationbasesfor AI solutions. Building on previous ESA work where security threats and mitigation measures for spacesystems were identified and considering emerging policies and regulations, this activity will develop an'MLSecOps' framework, i.e. a comprehensive set of practices and tools, processes, and datasets to addressnew vulnerabilities. These will be integrated with operational MLOps infrastructure and validated in a spacesystem context. The targeted space system applications may range from engineering aids to securitymonitoring solutions. The solution will be based on public standards and knowledge bases such as the ENISAreport "Cybersecurity of AI and Standardisation," MITRE ATLAS, and OWASP Gen AI Security Project. Theseoffer a rich list of vulnerabilities and controls without considering the required adaptations for space missionspecifics. normalized.description: The increasing deployment of satellites is raising concerns regarding their impact on ground- and space-based astronomical observations and the need to comply with emerging Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) requirements. Reliable assessment of spacecraft visibility requires accurate knowledge of the optical properties of external spacecraft materials and their environmental degradation over time. However, existing data are limited, fragmented and often unsuitable for consistent spacecraft-level brightness analyses. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a system-integrated European database of optical properties for spacecraft materials with potential observational impacts, including solar arrays, multilayer insulation, thermo-optical coatings, antennas and external optical elements. The activity shall establish the required material datasets, perform dedicated measurement and characterisationcampaigns, and integrate the resulting data into an open-access database supporting DQS compliance assessments and brightness prediction tools. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 7.

normalized.title: MULTI-BAND DUAL-BEAM C-TO-Q/V SATCOM ANALOGUE BEAMFORMING INTEGRATED CIRCUIT (ARTES AT 7B.091) - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
normalized.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a wideband analogue beamforming integrated circuit (BFIC) capable of covering the entire frequency range from Cto Q/V-band, with two beams. This BFIC will serve as a modular and scalable solution for user-terminal flat-panel arrays, enabling multi-band and multi-product compatibility.Targeted Improvements: - Frequency coverage extended from C-band to Q/V-band in a single BFIC.- Fostering high-volume production scalability and economies of scale.- Enhanced design modularity, enabling flat-panel antennas to scale in aperture size (same number of beams) and/or number of beams (same aperture).Description:Conventionally, different BFICs have been used in applications at different frequency bands, e.g., the C- to Q/V-bands relevant to satcom. Also, such conventional BFICs typically generate a single beam. To enable the use of thesame BFIC in a broad range of satcom products, this activity will develop a next-generation dual-beam analogue BFIC with wideband coverage from C- to Q/V-band. Thus, the envisioned BFIC will serve as a fundamental building block for future flat-panel antenna arrays, supporting scalable designs by allowing additional BFICs to be integrated based on performance requirements. The development of this BFIC shall leverage insights from recent state-of-the-art wideband single-/dual-beam BFICs, such as the C- to Ka-band BFICs, which are developed outside ESA Member States. These contributions highlight the growing industry demand for multi-beam and frequency-agnostic BFIC solutions, which can reduce system complexity and accelerate product development, with the potential for higher volumeproduction in comparison to single-band BFICs. Therefore, the envisioned BFIC will cover the entire C- to Q/V-band range and generatetwo beams, which will enable its reuse across multiple product lines and reduce the need for band-specific BFICs. The design willemphasise performance consistency across the wide frequency range, minimising variations in gain, noise figure, and linearity.Additionally, the activity will assess the thermal and power consumption challenges associated with multi-beam and broadband analogue BFICs at millimetre-wave frequencies, ensuring that the proposed solution is viable for both low- and high-end satcom applications. Successful execution will position Europe as a leader in wideband BFICs, securing our competitiveness in the evolving satcom ecosystem. The wideband analogue BFIC will be tested against DVB-S2/S2X or 5G-NR waveform in a relevant environment.
